Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll kick off in a sec, i see all the faces, Evan, Maya, Samir, uh quick round — we got Diego and Priya from our solutions team as well.
[00:15] Evan (NovaCore): hey thanks Aisha, excited to go through the integration checklist. we've been talking internally about listing on marketplace and we want to make sure the reference arch is clear for our customers.
[00:28] Diego (Redwood SE): yeah hi, hi, good to meet you all. i can walk through the networking and packaging suggestions from the Redwood side. quick note, sorry if i mumble, was just on another call.
[00:40] Maya (NovaCore): no worries. first, how does the marketplace listing tie into the Private and Dedicated options? we have customers with strict VPC requirements.
[00:50] Priya (Redwood): good question, so typically the marketplace listing will offer a few SKUs: hosted/api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployment — the private option points to our private control plane package + deployment artifacts. the listing itself links to the quickstart repo and the reference arch doc. (a bit of chatter)
[01:12] Samir (NovaCore): for private deployments we need to ensure KMS integration for keys and that audit logs are easy to ship to customer's SIEM. can you confirm what logs are available?
[01:22] Diego (Redwood SE): yes, we produce audit logs at the control plane level — auth events, model rollouts, usage metrics, and per-request traces. we support forwarding to S3 or customer SIEM via syslog/agents. also, KMS/HSM is supported for secrets, and we can outline the envelope encryption model in the ref arch.
[01:40] Evan (NovaCore): great. on the marketplace side, procurement asks about entitlements and billing integration — do you have a marketplace-compatible SKU we can reuse, or do we need to map to an AWS marketplace product?
[01:52] Aisha (Redwood): we can provide a canonical SKU mapping and pricing tiers; typically we provide per-token or per-concurrency pricing for hosted, and reserved GPU-hour pricing for Dedicated. for private we usually do a platform subscription + per-seat or per-throughput metric. we'll send a draft pricing sheet.
[02:10] Maya (NovaCore): ok that helps. another thing: NovaCore has a Terraform-based onboarding flow for infra. can the Redwood quickstart be a Terraform module so we can embed it into our landing zone?
[02:22] Priya (Redwood): absolutely, we have a Terraform module and cloudformation quickstart. Diego, i think you had notes about making the module param-friendly for VPC peering and route tables?
[02:32] Diego (Redwood SE): yes, the module exposes parameters for vpc_cidr, peering subnets, kms_key_arn, and allowed_cidrs for management plane. one caveat — if you want private data path we recommend using direct peering + transit gateway for lower latency. i've seen higher jitter when going over NAT with large token streaming. (murmur)
[02:54] Samir (NovaCore): streaming — that is important for the real-time features we demo. we have a latency target of 80-120ms p95 for short prompt flows. can Redwood meet that on Dedicated or Private?
[03:06] Diego (Redwood SE): yes on Dedicated with tuned GPUs and local routing we can meet sub-100ms p95 for typical Llama-like models at short sequences. for Private it depends on where the compute is — if it's colocated in the customer's VPC or on-prem with low network hops, we can hit it. also need to call out batching and KV cache behavior; those can change p95 if not configured.
[03:28] Evan (NovaCore): are there known gotchas for quantized models or custom model variants when running on Private?
[03:33] Priya (Redwood): compatibility varies; we test a matrix of quantization configs. some model optimizations need specific kernel paths — we'll include a compatibility table in the ref arch doc and the marketplace listing. sometimes transcriptions show model names weirdly, sorry.
[03:48] Maya (NovaCore): regarding security docs, we need SOC2/ISO statements, SSO/SAML integration steps, and RBAC mapping for our enterprise buyers.
[03:58] Aisha (Redwood): we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts; SAML SSO is supported and we can map SAML groups to RBAC roles in the console. we'll attach the security pack to the listing.
[04:12] Diego (Redwood SE): and for network security, we also provide an option for customer-managed NAT and we can restrict egress to a small set of IPs for licensing lookups. however, if you need fully air-gapped we have an on-prem package that needs additional ops work.
[04:33] Samir (NovaCore): perfect. pilot scope — proposal idea: private deployment in NovaCore staging VPC, run a 2-week pilot with a single model, 2 GPUs, benchmark throughput and latency, and validate logging and entitlements integration. if that passes, expand for marketplace public listing.
[04:52] Aisha (Redwood): sounds reasonable. action items: we'll send the marketplace listing draft and pricing SKUs; NovaCore to share terraform module; Diego to sketch a reference architecture with KMS and peering notes; Samir to confirm success criteria.
[05:06] Evan (NovaCore): timeline — can we aim to have the draft listing and ref arch by next week? procurement wants a rough pricing by then to start legal review.
[05:15] Aisha (Redwood): yes we'll aim for 8/18. Diego, Priya — can you have the ref arch and module notes by 8/19?
[05:22] Diego (Redwood SE): yep i can do that, i'll include notes about batching and KV cache settings for the pilot.
[05:29] Priya (Redwood): i'll also include a short checklist for the NovaCore ops team: network rules, KMS ARN, SAML metadata, and the initial entitlements mapping.
[05:38] Maya (NovaCore): one more question on marketplace listing: do you allow co-branded terms or is it Redwood-hosted only?
[05:45] Aisha (Redwood): typically the listing is co-branded; the procurement/legal language can be co-badged, and we can have NovaCore as the publisher in the marketplace if you prefer — we handle the integration and entitlements mapping. we'll surface options in the draft.
[05:58] Samir (NovaCore): ok great. any technical blockers we should raise now?
[06:03] Diego (Redwood SE): nothing immediate — just need the terraform module and the NovaCore network topology so i can validate peering and egress rules. also, if you plan to use a custom model, send us the model size and quant config so we can pre-validate kernels.
[06:18] Evan (NovaCore): noted. we'll share the module and topology by 8/20.
[06:24] Aisha (Redwood): wrap-up: recap next steps and owners. we'll also attach the shared artifacts: draft listing link, draft reference arch (diego/redwood edits), and quickstart terraform repo. links: (1) draft listing (placeholder) https://drive.redwood.ai/novacore-marketplace-draft, (2) quickstart terraform https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart-terraform, (3) ref-arch canvas in miro https://miro.com/app/novacore-ref-arch.
[06:50] Maya (NovaCore): thanks all — we'll review and come back with comments.
[06:55] Aisha (Redwood): thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the action items. bye.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few errors (product names, acronyms like KV cache sometimes split as K V cache). minor speaker attribution glitches around minute 2.
